title: Measurability of the single-vector distortion event
statement:
Fix a vector $x\in\bbr^d$ and a real number $\varepsilon$, and let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ be a measurable space. Suppose $A\colon\Omega\to\bbr^{k\times d}$ is a measurable map assigning to each $\omega$ a $k\times d$ real matrix $A(\omega)$. Then the set of outcomes on which $x$ is badly distorted,
\[
  \bigl\{\,\omega\in\Omega \;:\; \varepsilon\,\|x\|^2 < \bigl|\,\|A(\omega)\,x\|^2 - \|x\|^2\,\bigr|\,\bigr\},
\]
is measurable.
hypotheses_covered: A is a measurable map from Omega to k-by-d real matrices
x is a fixed vector in R^d
epsilon is a fixed real number
Omega carries a measurable space structure
replaced:
For any measurable map $A : \Omega \to \mathrm{Matrix}(\mathrm{Fin}\,k,
\mathrm{Fin}\,d,\mathbb{R})$, fixed $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and $\varepsilon \in
\mathbb{R}$, the set $\{\omega \mid \text{BadSingle}\;\varepsilon\;(A\,\omega)\;x\}$
is measurable.  The key step is that each coordinate map
$\omega \mapsto (A\,\omega \cdot \text{toEuclideanLin}\; x)_i$ is measurable, hence
so is the squared norm.
